title: Probabilistic Genetics and the Genetically Inherited Organism as a Probabilistic Computer Based on p-bits
content: This article describes and discusses profound analogies between the patterns found in the statistical organization of  nucleotide sequences of genomic DNAs and the mathematical framework of probabilistic computers based on probabilistic bits (p-bits). In such probabilistic computers, noise is utilized as a computational resource. The physical and mathematical foundations of these computers are linked to Maxwell-Boltzmann stochastic thermodynamics, the Ising model of spin glasses, and the symmetric energy landscapes of states within clusters of p-bits—referred to as "p-dits." The article presents analogous landscape symmetries existed in the statistical patterns of genomic DNA nucleotide sequences from both higher and lower organisms, as studied by the p-dit analyses method. These analogies form the basis for a model approach that treats the molecular-genetic information system as a thermodynamic, probabilistic-computational medium in which electromagnetic and other noises serve as a computational resource. In this approach, the author proposes a theory of the p-dit representation of probabilities in genetic informatics.
